text: It was a lonely trip, the weekday route from Boston to Provincetown and back, especially after Labor Day.
The badger inside of her just dug in its claws and that was that.
She loved stacking, and organizing her shabby little counter, which was already neat and wiped clean, though no one was around to see it.
The thin brick lanes were dimly purple in the setting dusk, and sugared with leaves the color of campfires.
Norah was a nester, and her instinct was to stuff a space with pillows and loveseats like she was stuffing a turkey.
Thom, her sad poet, a regular at the bar she tended on this lonely trip to land’s end.
A small avalanche of concern tumbled through her even before she saw the text.
Might as well get some studying done in her last moments on earth, she thought.
And so the apartment was a riot of bumblebee-colored throw pillows and Gothic little statues, a Bockler painting abutting a bouquet of peacock feathers.
The neighborhood was absurdly romantic, especially now, but also a little melancholy; shadows from the kindled streetlights gathered in doorways and alleys, like mourners lining up to hail her.
I need you to understand the, like, ecosystem we’re both in when it comes to decisions.
It was extremely theirs, a spooky little salon that was close to all of their work obligations and somehow also affordable.
Norah was scared out of her mind and wild with love.
Drew’s eyes in the low light promised accountability, expectations, the brine of love and justice.
Sometimes she would be upended across Drew’s lap right away, but usually there was a discussion first.
What are you about to get, Norah Dorothea?
I want you in that corner, and I want you thinking about what you did, why it matters, and what’s about to happen.
Norah shivered despite having ticked up the thermostat before Drew had come home, knowing that spankings always made her cold.
What do you get when you’re extra naughty, young lady?
I’m going to hammer whatever nails need hammering until this behavior starts to change.
It wasn’t that she was bad. It was that she was quite good, and quite underperforming.
Now the guilt was less like rippling waves and more like a million little crabs.
Drew held out her hand and said “come,” and Norah walked over and took it, and was pulled into the bedroom and over Drew’s lap.
Witness, imaginary audience, the wages of this woman’s crimes: the scumbled rose of her backside, her hot tears.
Drew loved, even in this moment of discipline, the way Norah’s butt responded to a spanking, the tide of pink that spread across the lush white bay and then deepened into red.
Then it did, and down she fell into a bright room of pain.
